stimuli.description: 360-degree visuals and 3D sounds of four worship spaces (two mosques, two churches) in dry and wet acoustic conditions. Dry recordings had T30 < 0.4s, wet recordings had T30 ≥ 1.7s. Sound sources were Quran recitations for mosques and Christian hymns for churches.

limitations: Some results are specific to worship spaces and may not generalize to other building types.
Further studies are needed to examine the possibility of different frequency bands enhancing other kinds of emotions beyond spiritual emotions.
The binaural recording method used in Phase 1 did not account for head movement, which could impact the characteristics of the acoustic environment.

The developed multiple convolution method for room modes, when used in simulation, provides an estimation of general frequency bands where modes occur, and identifying absolute modes would be more accurate with recorded Impulse Responses.
Auralization technology may not provide a realistic representation of the acoustic environment at low frequencies, which are critical in worship spaces.
